A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CoPE study. Their complete main texts, appendices, equations, figures and tables support reliable matching and comparison. The disclosed uncertainty about some PDDL3 model identities limits those comparisons, rather than document completeness.

before.justification: v1 reports original planning correctness, constraint-category, error and robustness experiments in Section 6 and Appendix E.

after.justification: v2 retains original experiments and adds PDDL3 and newer-model results, plus a validation audit in Section 8.

M1.justification: v2 adds a PDDL3 formalization path: generated or edited PDDL3 is compiled through TCORE before planning and validation, with compiler- and solver-error repair prompts. This extends the existing generation/editing/revision framework without redesigning its other procedures.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate BlocksWorld-100, CoinCollector-100, BlocksWorld-XL-100 and MysteryBlocksWorld-100, retaining the complexity and lexical-obfuscation scenarios. LTL remains restricted to CoinCollector goal, action and state constraints. Additional models and formalisms do not introduce new task coverage.

E2.justification: v2 adds PDDL3 comparisons with generation/editing and revision variants, Gemini-3-Flash, and DeepSeek-V3.2 Thinking and Non-Thinking configurations. Conversely, the PDDL generation-plus-revision and editing-plus-revision comparisons on XL and Mystery datasets in v1 Tables 5–6 are absent from v2 Tables 12–13.

E3.justification: v2 introduces explicit Thinking versus Non-Thinking evaluation conditions for DeepSeek-V3.2 and a validation audit reported on 20 samples. The existing benchmark subsets and correctness metric remain. The explanation that revision repairs syntax rather than permitting replanning clarifies the existing procedure.

E4.justification: Existing constraint-category and error analyses are extended to PDDL3 and newer models, and Section 8 adds a small audit of false-positive plan validation. Complexity and lexical robustness analyses remain, although their appendix results lose the revision-assisted PDDL variants.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run evaluation protocols, confidence intervals, significance tests or comparable uncertainty estimates. The added validation audit reports an observation without statistical uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: v2 adds extensive PDDL3 and newer-model scores and aggregate LTL results in Table 11. Retained robustness values also change: DeepSeek-R1 planner correctness on XL changes from 43/30 to 44/31, and DeepSeek-V3 on Mystery from 11/6 to 11/15, ordered unconstrained/constrained. Revision-assisted robustness entries are removed. These are reporting changes, not established methodological performance gains.

T1.justification: v1 asserts constraint-category completeness informally; v2 Appendix F adds Definitions 7–8, Theorem 1 and a case-based completeness proof. Section 3 also formalizes category exclusions and introduces a non-destructive qualification. The proof additionally excludes constraints eliminating all valid traces, making this more than a notation revision.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the central contribution: CoPE introduces four categories of natural-language constraints that challenge planning/formalization and undermine robustness to complexity and lexical shifts. PDDL3 and newer-model experiments broaden the supporting evidence without replacing these claims.

C2.justification: v2 adds explanations linking PDDL3 failures to compilation errors and limited pretraining exposure, qualifies the complexity finding for Gemini, and acknowledges uncertain DeepSeek identities. Section 8 infers negligible false positives from 20 inspected samples and adds claims that formalization mitigates downstream safety risks. These substantially expand interpretations and validity qualifications.

D1.justification: Appendix D adds PDDL3, SMT and LTL prompt listings, including compiler-repair instructions and the previously undisclosed SMT 100-step limit. v2 also documents annotation authorship/procedure, clarifies syntax-revision attempts and discloses DeepSeek API-version ambiguity. Existing LTL implementation prose is relocated rather than newly introduced.

R1.justification: v2 adds six references covering PDDL3 foundations, TCORE, domain-model alignment, DeepSeek-V3.2 and agent safety. Section 2 explicitly positions CoPE against classical PDDL3 constraint work, while the broader literature discussion and related-work comparison table remain.

P1.justification: v2 edits terminology and prose, revises the constraint explanation and error-analysis heading, moves existing LTL details into Section 5, and reorganizes appendices. The main section sequence and substantial passages and example listings are retained.

P2.justification: Performance, category, robustness and error plots are extensively redrawn for additional series; the LTL plot becomes full-width. The appendix error-example figure moves into the main text and gains PDDL3 panels. Combined result tables are reorganized into method-specific tables, substantially changing the visual presentation.

improvement.justification: The PDDL3/newer-model comparisons and substantially fuller prompt documentation improve empirical usefulness and reproducibility. The net gain is limited by uncertain PDDL3 model identities, removal of revision-assisted robustness results, and the unsupported inference that zero false positives in 20 samples establishes a negligible rate. The new proof also excludes constraints eliminating all plans, conflicting with the unsolvable cases retained in Table 1 and Section 4.
